Let the cube have centre at the origin and vertices \((\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)\).  
For a vertex with sign vector \(v=(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)\), the plane through its three adjacent vertices has equation
\[
\varepsilon_1 x+\varepsilon_2 y+\varepsilon_3 z=1.
\]
The centre \((0,0,0)\) lies on the side
\[
\varepsilon_1 x+\varepsilon_2 y+\varepsilon_3 z\le 1.
\]
Taking all eight vertices gives all sign choices, which is equivalent to
\[
|x|+|y|+|z|\le 1.
\]
This inequality describes a regular octahedron. Its six vertices are \((\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1)\), i.e. the centres of the six faces of the original cube.

\[
